findings.evidence: Table 3-3, row 'total parameters', dense 70B column: '70B ... [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]' in the derivation column, while the dense column label reads 'canonical scenario'. The book's own convention (Ch 4, Table 4-2 note 1): 'an input or parameter assumption (traffic, latency target, price, token count) is [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]'. Table 4-2 row 'Model parameters 70B' is correctly labeled [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION].
findings.issue: Evidence-label mismatch: the 70B total-parameters figure in Table 3-3's dense column carries [DERIVED] epistemic status but is actually a chosen input (the canonical teaching model's parameter count), so its epistemic status should be [ASSUMPTION], not [DERIVED]. This is an internal inconsistency with Table 4-2, which correctly labels the same 70B value as [ASSUMPTION].
findings.fix_instruction: Change the dense-column label for the 'total parameters' row in Table 3-3 from [canonical scenario][DERIVED] to [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION], consistent with Table 4-2's 'Model parameters 70B' row.

findings.evidence: Table 3-1, row 'Active parameters per token', value '70B', derivation: 'All parameters active for every token (dense) [canonical scenario][DERIVED]'. The value is the same 70B assumed parameter count restated, not an independent arithmetic result.
findings.issue: Evidence-label mismatch: the 70B active-parameter count in Table 3-1's dense column is labeled [DERIVED] but is a restatement of the assumed 70B parameter count (Table 4-2 correctly labels the 70B input as [ASSUMPTION]). Per the book's convention, a chosen input is [ASSUMPTION] and only an arithmetic result from assumed inputs is [DERIVED].
findings.fix_instruction: Change the epistemic-status label for the 'Active parameters per token' row in Table 3-1 from [canonical scenario][DERIVED] to [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION], since the value restates the assumed parameter count rather than computing a new quantity from it.

findings.issue: The two KV-cache rows of Table 3-3 carry a single row-level [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] tag, but their dense-column values (~24.1 GB FP16 / ~12.06 GB at 8-bit for 9,200 tokens) are the canonical scenario's own derived quantities — labeled [canonical scenario][DERIVED] for the identical computation in Ch 4 Table 4-2, Ch 5 Table 5-2 and Ch 7 Table 7-1 — and every other dense/MoE row in this same table splits the tags per column. As printed, these two rows downgrade the dense column's provenance to ILLUSTRATIVE, contradicting both the table's own footer convention and the book-wide labeling of the same numbers.
findings.fix_instruction: Split the inline tags on the two KV rows exactly as the residency/weight-read/FLOPs rows do — e.g. "[canonical scenario][DERIVED] (dense column) · [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] (MoE column)" — or explicitly scope the trailing [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] to the MoE value only.
